RENDER SPEC for a real font-embedding press PDF produced through a full print engine (must convert cleanly to native InDesign). Trim: 4 x 6 inches portrait (1200 x 1800 px at 300 ppi) box-end film-roll label. Palette: Graphite Black #191C21 ink on Titanium White #F3F4F5 stock, one Guard Bronze #B08A54 hairline rule. Typography: tight modern grotesque for tier name and headings, clean humanist sans for the performance rows and body.

CRITICAL STRUCTURE: author the tier name, the width-and-length line, the six performance rows and the warranty statement as ONE SINGLE CONTINUOUS TEXT STORY in one text frame (no separate frame per field) — a single flowing block where each field is a run inside one story, separated by paragraph and tab characters. The small Apexguard mark sits in its own graphic frame at top; the reference/SKU code sits in its own small text frame at the very bottom. Everything between them is the one continuous story.

Story order (top to bottom, all inside the one frame):
[MARK graphic frame, ~180px tall, top-centered]
TIER NAME (large, e.g. 'Guard Elite')
WIDTH & LENGTH LINE (e.g. '48 in x 100 ft')
PERFORMANCE (six rows, tab between label and value):
  Film gauge\t8.0 mil
  Clarity retained\t92%
  Self-healing topcoat\tYes
  Hydrophobic contact angle\t110 deg
  UV rejection\t99%
  Finish\tGloss
WARRANTY (this run sits in a FIXED-MEASURE text frame exactly 3 short lines tall, sized to a ~12-word statement; longer statements silently truncate at the last line):
  'Ten year limited warranty against yellowing, cracking, peeling and delamination.'
DEALER PRICE line (e.g. '$3,760 / roll')
[SKU / REFERENCE CODE small text frame at bottom, e.g. 'AG-GE-48']

Populate the sample render with the Guard Elite 48in values above. The warranty frame's measure must be locked so that if a warranty statement four times longer is flowed in later, the text simply stops at the third line with no visible spill, no overset marker and no error.

assets.content:
Apexguard Surface Systems - direction for the rollout

Premium, modern, performance automotive. Minimalist and confident. Not flashy, not factory catalog, not tuner.

No mascots. No vintage badges. No heavy gradients. No starbursts, no percentage flashes, no chrome bevels, no exclamation points. We state numbers and let them carry.

A full install runs eighteen hundred to six thousand dollars on a car worth sixty thousand, so it has to look like that. A dealer principal has to believe the ten year warranty printed beside the film, and a two hundred dollar tint-shop flyer kills that. Equally, do not push it into moody enthusiast car-culture; we are a supplier a dealer group puts on its reconditioning line, not an Instagram page.

The master mark and the three tier marks (Guard, Guard Pro, Guard Elite) have to read as one family. A dealer looks at all four and sees one supplier, not three products.

One restrained accent against a deep neutral. Confident spacing. Performance stated as a plain table, not a burst. Photography clean and even, not dramatic.

If anything in our data looks wrong to you, tell us before it prints.
